summary.intent: Evaluate whether a two-phase search analysis (cheap file score first, then analyze only the top K files) could speed up monokl's search pipeline without changing result quality, via a prototype on an experiment branch delegated to a subagent.
summary.outcome: The subagent's prototype failed its gates: top-50 rows changed on broad queries (rank 1 included) and speedup was under 2x at best. Nothing was pushed and no PR was made; the prototype remains uncommitted in a worktree.

repo: Text search and the file walk dominate latency in monokl, not parsing; `rg` alone takes about 364 ms on the 20k-file set.
The quality harness `rg-compare.py` is weak evidence for batching because most of its queries have fewer than 100 eligible files and never reach the batching path.
The harness scores fd at 0 because this main branch has no Rust analyzer.
BM25 statistics and name boosts depend on the analyzed set, so a safe bound on the remaining files' scores cannot be computed cheaply.
The prototype added the knobs `MONOKL_FIRST_BATCH` (`all` or a number, sets K) and `MONOKL_TRACE` (prints files analyzed vs eligible), plus a debug env var `MONOKL_DEBUG_ORDER`.

code.finding: File modified by the two-phase search prototype; changes are uncommitted on `experiment/two-phase-search` and include the `MONOKL_DEBUG_ORDER` debug env var that must be removed if the work is kept.

workflow: Subagent results are reported as hand-back text and carry no user authority; they should be treated as information, not approval.
Measure speedups with a release build and the median of many runs (15 here), and compare top-N row identity across K values, not just aggregate quality metrics.
Isolating experiments in an agent worktree on an experiment branch keeps failed prototypes out of main.

friction: The harness has weak coverage for the batching path because most queries have fewer than 100 eligible files.
K=100 truncation changed top-10 results for 11 of 25 truncated queries on zustand/zod/axios and rank 1 for 4 of 30 queries on the TypeScript repo.
Speedups were inconsistent: some cases slowed down (zod `type` 0.88x, axios `string` 0.91x).
A declaration-line signal in the phase-1 score reduced top-10 misses from 4 to 2 of 25 queries but did not fully fix the problem.
`just ci` was not run on the prototype.
open_items: Decide whether to discard the `experiment/two-phase-search` worktree or keep it; if kept, remove the `MONOKL_DEBUG_ORDER` env var.
Record the decision-log bullets: two-phase analysis rejected, text search bounds latency, and no cheap safe bound exists on remaining files.
Consider targeting text search and the file walk for future latency work instead of analysis batching.
Optionally extend the quality harness with queries that have more than 100 eligible files so batching is actually exercised.
